mappings.note: What the shehnai and Kashi were to him ('jannat se badhkar') -- the text says so in as many words. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the phrase is quoted, not appraised as style.

Yatindra Mishra's own birth year and birthplace -- author biography, not the content of the prose piece. The frame carries no biography/literary-history LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because it is defined over the vishayvastu of the prescribed prose.
Whom the lesson is written about (Ustad Bismillah Khan) -- basic comprehension of the text's subject. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, which would apply if the vidha or the writer's purpose were being asked.
Bhimpalasi and Multani identified as raags -- a term's sense in context. Rejected C-H1.2 since no grammatical structure is tested.
The shehnai's sound called mangal dhwani -- stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2; recall, not appreciation.
The route to the Balaji temple he preferred (past Rasoolan/Batoolan Bai's house). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- narrative detail.
What he has been asking for across eighty years (sur). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the answer is a stated fact, while the thematic reading of it is tested by separate items.
Where he did his riyaz (Balaji temple) -- content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, nothing authorial at stake.
He regarded shehnai and Kashi as jannat on this earth -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 for the same reason as its near-twin item 61.
Which instrument he played on Muharram (the shehnai, for the nauha). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- factual.
The reed used to play the shehnai -- technical detail from the lesson. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no craft question.

Who wrote 'Naubatkhane mein Ibaadat' -- attribution of the piece to Yatindra Mishra, i.e. literary-history knowledge about the writer rather than the text's content. The frame has no biography/authorship LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because it covers the vishayvastu of the prose, not who produced it.
What a 'naubatkhana' is -- a word's meaning in context. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the shirshak ki saarthakta question would be LO-2, but this only asks the word's sense.

Meaning of 'ibaadat' (pooja) as used in the title and text -- contextual word meaning. Rejected C-H1.2: although the word is Urdu, the item is not a vyakaran exercise on Urdu-Farsi vocabulary, it is comprehension of the term the lesson turns on.
Where his naana played the shehnai (Balaji temple). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- straight recall.
The family trade of Ali Bakhsh's line (shehnai vaadan) -- content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no interpretation.
State of Amiruddin's birth (Bihar) -- a fact about the text's subject. Rejected C-H1.3 competency, which is reserved for the writer's own life.
His ancestral village, Dumraon -- content. Rejected C-H1.3 competency for the same reason: this is the subject's biography, which the lesson itself supplies.
Age at which he came to Kashi (six). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- numeric recall.
His father's name, Paigambar Bakhsh -- stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3 competency: Bismillah Khan's family is the text's content, not the author's biography.
Why the boy went to the Balaji temple (to practise). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the reason is stated, not inferred from the writer's standpoint.
What he begged for in sajda (a true sur) -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2; the 'music as worship' reading is tested elsewhere, this item only recalls the act.
His belief in Khuda's power to grant -- content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no craft or intent question.
The proper way to give daad ('waah') as the lesson records it. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- recall of a stated custom.
Which jayanti is observed at the Balaji/Hanuman temple. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- factual.
The Son river's banks as the source of narkat grass -- stated detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no interpretation.
Who kindled his early musical interest (Rasoolan and Batoolan Bai). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- content recall.
His favourite actress, Sulochana -- a fact the lesson gives. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, nothing authorial.

What his life inspires -- keyed to fraternity across communities, which is the message the writer builds the portrait to deliver. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no single stated fact yields it; the reader must grasp the piece's intent.

Explicitly 'lekhak ne aisa kyon kaha' about Kashi waking and sleeping on music -- the writer's own figure and his reason for it. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1, which fits the companion item that merely recalls the statement.
Why Bismillah Khan will always be remembered -- the writer's summing-up verdict on his subject. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the options are competing evaluations, not recallable facts.
Sense of the phrase 'sur ki tameez' in context (understanding of music). Rejected C-H1.2 -- a contextual phrase meaning, not a muhavara/vyakaran drill.
Where the annual Kashi music gathering is held (Sankat Mochan). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 -- place recall.
Five days of the Sankat Mochan sabha -- numeric fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no interpretation.
How long a reed takes to soften (15-20 minutes) -- stated detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 for the same reason.

How he showed reverence to Kashi Vishwanath (turning the shehnai towards Kashi) -- a described action. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the gesture is reported, not being read as authorial symbolism here.
Which tradition the extract describes (sangeet aayojan) -- 'lekhak ne varnan kiya' is plain content recall here. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as neither intent nor style is appraised.

Why the shastras call Kashi 'Anandkanan' -- explained from reasons the lesson supplies, and the epithet is attributed to the shastras, not coined by the writer. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, which fits epithets that are Yatindra Mishra's own.
Two-mark explanation of 'sur ki tameez' -- contextual sense of a phrase from the text. Rejected C-H1.2 since it is not a vyakaran item; stem misprints 'sur' as 'soor'.
Why Amiruddin liked passing the two sisters' house and how Balaji's dyodhi gained -- both halves answered from narrated content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because no authorial purpose is under discussion.

Asks the student to argue the piece's central proposition -- art practised as worship, which is what the title 'Naubatkhane mein Ibaadat' asserts. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the task is to defend the writer's thesis, not to reproduce incidents.
Establish that he was a true human being -- a character sketch assembled from incidents in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the evidence is content, and the writer's craft is not the object.
Khan Sahib's greatest gift -- the lesson states it directly (the lifelong jijivisha to learn music whole). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the verdict is quoted from the text.

Why Kashi is CALLED a school of culture -- interpreting the writer's metaphor, matching the MCQ of the same wording. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1, which fits the plain 'Kashi kiski paathshala hai' recall item.

Why the shehnai would have earned the title 'shah' among sushir vaadya -- reasoned from the instrument's properties as the lesson describes them. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the title is a traditional one the writer reports.

Which traits of his personality impressed you and which you would adopt -- abhivyakti built on the text's content, which LO-1 explicitly covers. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the response is about the man, not about how the writer wrote him.

Names the writer and asks on what grounds HE claims Khan Sahib will always be music's nayak -- squarely lekhak ka mantavya. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the question is about the author's reasoning, not the subject's life.
Illustrate his reverence for Kashi Vishwanath and the Balaji temple with examples -- pure evidence-gathering from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no appraisal of style.
Write three traits of his that impress you -- content-based expression. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the traits belong to the subject, not to the writing.
What Khan Sahib used to reminisce about -- a list recoverable from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, nothing authorial.
Which things of Kashi come to mind -- drawn from the lesson's own catalogue of the city. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because it asks for content, not for what the writer meant by assembling it.
Describe his attachment to Muharram from the text -- narrative content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no intent or style question is posed.
Throw light on his simplicity -- character description evidenced from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the simplicity is the man's, not the prose's.
Two reasons he would not leave Kashi -- stated reasons. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the 'kyon' is settled by content.

Asks what relation the WRITER draws between the deer and Bismillah Khan -- an authorial image, i.e. bhasha-shaili and mantavya. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because there is no deer in the events of his life; the link exists only in the writing.
Which changes in Kashi distressed him -- stated in the text (the fading of music, adab, the old traditions). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, recall rather than appraisal.
How he spent what he earned playing at the temple -- content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, no craft question.

Sandarbh-prasang on the quoted 'phata sur na bakhshe...' line -- who said it to whom and why, answered from the episode. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because it asks the context of the speech, not an appreciation of the writer's idiom.
Why Dumraon is remembered in the shehnai world -- three reasons the text supplies. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the answer is entirely factual.
Why he felt such love for Kashi -- reasons given in the lesson. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the writer's own purpose is not what is being asked.
